estimands.outcome: First occurrence of the composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, or hospitalisation for heart failure
estimands.timepoint: trial-defined time-to-first-event follow-up; exact CV-composite follow-up is not normalised in the object, which records the registered primary-outcome timeframes as an average 32 months for FIDELIO-DKD and average study duration 41 months for FIGARO-DKD
estimands.missing_data_model: trial-reported time-to-first-event analysis in all randomised participants as posted by the registry; censoring and any imputation follow the trial source and are not reconstructed by this protocol

harmonisation_rule.harmonised_endpoint: Use the time-to-first-event cardiovascular composite with the same four components and order recorded for both trials: cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, or hospitalisation for heart failure. Do not silently pool kidney composites, all-cause mortality, all-cause hospitalisation, UACR, recurrent events, win ratios, or fixed-time dichotomous effects with this estimand.

eligibility.population: adults with chronic kidney disease and type 2 diabetes
eligibility.design: phase 3 randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven trial

statistics.small_k_ci_rule: HKSJ t_{k-1}, floor 1, reported alongside the unadjusted Wald interval when k is small

disclosure_clause.text: AUTHORED 2026-09-09, RETROSPECTIVE. The review answer was already knowable when these methods were chosen: a page on this topic had already been served, the canonical object records k = 2, and it records a pooled HR of 0.8655 with 95% CI 0.7877 to 0.951 for the cardiovascular composite. This is therefore an honest retrospective methods declaration for a rebuild, not a prospective pre-specification. REML and the small-k HKSJ sensitivity are declared because the existing object itself records REML, k = 2, and the small-k interval issue.

absolute_effect.control_risk_source: per-trial placebo-arm event counts and analysed denominators for cv_composite_first, with HR-based inference kept primary
